First, simplify the product using prime factors:

\[
2^3 \cdot 4^5 \cdot 6^7 \cdot 8^9
\]

Since \(4=2^2\), \(6=2\cdot 3\), and \(8=2^3\),

\[
2^3 \cdot (2^2)^5 \cdot (2\cdot 3)^7 \cdot (2^3)^9
\]

\[
= 2^3 \cdot 2^{10} \cdot 2^7 \cdot 3^7 \cdot 2^{27}
\]

\[
= 2^{3+10+7+27} \cdot 3^7 = 2^{47} \cdot 3^7
\]

Now compute modulo \(13\).

Since \(2^{12} \equiv 1 \pmod{13}\), and \(47 \equiv 11 \pmod{12}\),

\[
2^{47} \equiv 2^{11} \pmod{13}
\]

Also,

\[
2^6 = 64 \equiv 12 \equiv -1 \pmod{13}
\]

so

\[
2^{11} = 2^6 \cdot 2^5 \equiv (-1)\cdot 32 \equiv -32 \equiv -6 \equiv 7 \pmod{13}
\]

Next,

\[
3^3 = 27 \equiv 1 \pmod{13}
\]

so

\[
3^7 = 3^{6}\cdot 3 \equiv 1\cdot 3 \equiv 3 \pmod{13}
\]

Therefore,

\[
2^{47}\cdot 3^7 \equiv 7\cdot 3 \equiv 21 \equiv 8 \pmod{13}
\]

The answer is 8.
